questions.question: Why is returning no suggestion a healthy degraded mode for Smart Compose?
options: It avoids all model evaluation and capacity planning.
A completion is optional, so suppressing late, unsafe, stale, or weak output protects the typing experience.
It guarantees the writer will compose the same text without assistance.
It permits the service to skip privacy checks during overload.
questions.explanation: The product does not require output for every request. Suppression is safer than interrupting the writer with an invalid completion.

questions.question: The scenario has 150M concurrent compose sessions and 20 eligible typing events per minute. Client checks suppress 75% of those events. What average inference rate remains?
options: 3.125M requests/s
12.5M requests/s
25M requests/s
50M requests/s
questions.explanation: 150M x 20 / 60 = 50M raw opportunities/s; retaining 25% leaves 12.5M inference requests/s.

questions.question: A quality model produces the best offline score but pushes end-to-end p95 to 128 ms. What is the most defensible default-path decision?
options: Always serve it because quality metrics dominate latency.
Remove the output safety stage to recover the budget.
Route the default path to a faster tier and use the quality model only when measured headroom permits.
Queue every request until the quality model is available.
questions.explanation: Model routing should satisfy the complete user-visible budget. Optional quality work cannot make the default suggestion late.

questions.question: Why is general document retrieval not part of the default Smart Compose path?
options: Retrieval can never improve text generation.
The bounded draft and recent thread already provide the core completion context, while retrieval adds latency and privacy boundaries.
Transformer models cannot consume retrieved text.
Retrieval is always more expensive than model inference.
questions.explanation: RAG should answer a demonstrated information need. Ordinary phrase completion primarily depends on local, permissioned writing context.

questions.question: A candidate improves aggregate accepted characters, but unsafe output exceeds the hard gate for a multilingual slice. What should the release owner do?
options: Launch globally because the aggregate primary metric improved.
Hide the slice result and increase the sample size later.
Hold exposure for the failing slice or candidate until the safety regression is resolved.
Lower the safety threshold so more suggestions are displayed.
questions.explanation: A useful aggregate effect does not override a hard safety gate. Slice failures must remain visible in the release decision.

questions.question: Which measurement best connects serving cost to user value?
options: Peak GPU utilization only
Number of model parameters
Cost per accepted character
Total suggestions generated, whether displayed or not
questions.explanation: Cost per accepted character exposes wasted inference from weak requests, poor completions, and unnecessarily expensive model tiers.
